newsitem.title: UK: LIFFE coffee pares gains in switch-dominated trade.
newsitem.headline: LIFFE coffee pares gains in switch-dominated trade.

text.p: LIFFE robusta coffee futures reached Friday's mid-session with pared gains, but business was very slow and dominated by switch trades, floor sources said.
After a positive start, late morning profit-taking emerged to shave prices from their highs.
September was traded from a high of $1,895 -- the opening price -- to a low of $1,870, before finishing $16 higher at $1,876.
Turnover was 2,164 lots and the bulk of business was in spread trading. July/Sept traded up to $28 and Sept/Nov at $20. Further bids were seen at $25 and offers at $19.
Chart analysts expected the market to move in a wide $1,700-$2,000 band basis September in the absence of major market-moving news.
No major cold is in sight in Brazil's coffee areas in the next three to five days.
Private U.S. forecaster Weather Services Corp said temperatures were forecast near normal on Friday and above normal on Saturday and through to Tuesday.
Conditions were generally favourable for the trees but some disruptions to the harvest were still expected from scattered showers.
Elsewhere, Indonesian traders said there had been no news of robusta contract defaults by local firms, who were mostly holding off deals in anticipation of increases in London.
